quality.reason: Well-formatted whale transfer alerts with verifiable links, USD sizing, and engagement metrics, but the signals are homogeneous (all @whale_alert routine BTC exchange flows) with no directional analysis, deduplication, or source diversity to distinguish genuine signal from routine institutional operations.

Well-structured monitoring report with real quantitative data (PnL, win rate, OI, funding rates, fleet health) and relevant news, but empty ticker tags [[]] on two news items, no alert flagging on negative PnL (-$317.96 with 44% WR), and headlines lack actionable trade framing.
Well-structured quantitative review with clear position status, strategy scores, winner-runner-up margins, and score trends providing actionable signals for strategy selection decisions.

Well-structured with a genuine actionable anomaly (HYPE 75% bid-weighted orderbook + negative funding suggesting squeeze potential) and a promising BTC whale squeeze alert, but most table rows show neutral readings (~50% book, near-zero funding) that add routine noise rather than signal, and the core whale details are truncated.

Dense, well-structured review with quantified per-agent metrics, trend deltas, and clear status flags that pinpoint specific failures (news regression, 53-day stale trader at -$483, meta-agent idle 137 days with 0 briefs), giving directly actionable triage targets despite minor issues like the contradictory 0%-uptime-but-106-scans reading and lack of explicit remediation steps.

Well-structured scan with transparent methodology, dedup/relevance scoring, proper arXiv links/dates/categories, and a topically relevant lead paper (LLM-agent trading research), though the truncated preview and slight stock-vs-crypto scope drift leave minor uncertainty.

Coordinated multi-market repricing with specific probabilities, change deltas, and volume context makes this genuinely actionable signal rather than noise, though it lacks catalyst context and includes one thin-volume ($44K) market.
